title: "Get started"
---

```{python}
#| include: false
# Setup, hidden from readers. Every .qmd page starts with this same cell
# (tests/test_docs_pages.py checks). It works in a fresh folder, reads the
# example project from this repository's tests/data (offline), and defines
# sh(), which runs a command shown on the page and prints its output.
import os
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import warnings
from pathlib import Path

import useful_views

_mirror = Path(useful_views.__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "tests" / "data"
if not (_mirror / "examples" / "pwt").is_dir():
    raise RuntimeError(f"no example data at {_mirror}")
os.environ["USEFUL_VIEWS_DATA_URL"] = str(_mirror)
os.environ.update(NO_COLOR="1", PYTHON_COLORS="0", COLUMNS="100", PYTHONUNBUFFERED="1", PYTHONIOENCODING="utf-8")
WORK = str(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="useful-views-docs-")).resolve())
os.chdir(WORK)
warnings.formatwarning = lambda message, category, *args, **kwargs: f"{category.__name__}: {message}\n"


def sh(line, expect=0):
    """Run one command shown on the page (useful-views, cd or cat) and print
    its output as a terminal would. Fails if it exits with another code."""
    word, _, rest = line.partition(" ")
    if word == "cd":
        os.chdir(shlex.split(rest)[0])
        return
    if word == "cat":
        print(Path(shlex.split(rest)[0]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"), end="")
        return
    if word != "useful-views":
        raise ValueError(f"sh() runs useful-views, cd and cat, not {line!r}")
    done = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "useful_views", *shlex.split(rest)],
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, encoding="utf-8",
    )
    out = done.stdout.replace(WORK, "/path/to")
    if out.strip():
        print(out, end="")
    if done.returncode != expect:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{line!r} exited with {done.returncode}, not {expect}:\n{out}")
```

This page takes you through a small project from start to finish. You get
an example, make its views, look at one, and write a recipe of your own.
Everything runs in a terminal. [From Python](guides/python.qmd) does the
same in a notebook.

You need useful-views and polars in one Python environment.
[Installation](installation.md) shows how.

## Get the example

```sh
useful-views example pwt
cd pwt-example
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
sh("useful-views example pwt")
sh("cd pwt-example")
```

The example holds real data: an extract of the Penn World Table 11.0 for
Brazil, Germany, Spain and the United States. Its `README.md` gives the
source and how to cite it. The project looks like this:

```text
pwt-example/
├── README.md          what the project is, and the data credit
├── AGENTS.md          instructions for AI coding assistants
├── sources.toml       where each raw file comes from
├── datapackage.json   the record of what each recipe made
├── raw/               the files you start from
│   └── pwt110_bra_deu_esp_usa.csv
├── recipes/
│   ├── pwt_panel/     recipe.toml and three steps
│   └── gdp_per_capita/
├── work/              in-between files, one folder per recipe
└── useful-views/      the views, and README.md, their catalog
```

```{python}
#| include: false
# The tree above is what example made.
assert {"README.md", "AGENTS.md", "sources.toml", "datapackage.json", "raw", "recipes", "work", "useful-views"} <= set(os.listdir())
assert sorted(os.listdir("recipes")) == ["gdp_per_capita", "pwt_panel"]
assert len(os.listdir("recipes/pwt_panel")) == 4  # recipe.toml and three steps
```

## The words

useful-views is meant to be easy! It uses a few (hopefully) useful words:

| Word | What it is | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **Raw input** | A file you start from. No recipe makes it. | `raw/` |
| **Step** | A Python script that makes at least one real change to the data. | a numbered file in a recipe folder |
| **Recipe** | Steps that run in order. From the inputs it lists, it makes the views it lists. | a folder in `recipes/` |
| **View** | A table a recipe makes: a useful view. | `useful-views/` |
| **Work** | In-between files that only the later steps of the same recipe read. | `work/<recipe>/` |

## Make the views

```sh
useful-views sync
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
sh("useful-views sync")
```

`sync` ran both recipes, upstream first: `gdp_per_capita` reads the view
that `pwt_panel` makes. It recorded what each recipe read and made in
`datapackage.json`, and listed the views in the catalog,
`useful-views/README.md`.

```sh
useful-views check
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
sh("useful-views check")
```

`check` reports anything missing, refused or out of date. It changes
nothing.

## Look at a view

Views are parquet files, so any library can read them:

```{python}
import polars as pl

gdp = pl.read_parquet("useful-views/gdp-per-capita.parquet")
gdp.filter(pl.col("year") == 2023)
```

## Write a recipe

Add a recipe that averages each country's growth since 2000. Start from the
template:

```sh
useful-views new-recipe growth_since_2000
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
sh("useful-views new-recipe growth_since_2000")
```

Run it before you fill it in:

```sh
useful-views run growth_since_2000
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
sh("useful-views run growth_since_2000", expect=3)
```

The template still says TODO, so `run` refuses before anything changes. The
message names the file to fix, each problem, and the rule.

Fix it in your editor. Rename `01_first_step.py` to `01_average_growth.py`,
then make the two files say this:

```{python}
#| include: false
# What the reader writes in their editor.
recipe = Path("recipes/growth_since_2000")
(recipe / "recipe.toml").write_text(
    'description = "Average annual growth of GDP per capita since 2000."\n'
    'inputs  = ["useful-views/gdp-per-capita.parquet"]\n'
    'outputs = ["useful-views/growth-since-2000.parquet"]\n'
    "\n"
    "[[steps]]\n"
    'file = "01_average_growth.py"\n'
    'description = "Average the growth of GDP per capita by country, from 2000 on."\n',
    encoding="utf-8",
)
(recipe / "01_first_step.py").unlink()
(recipe / "01_average_growth.py").write_text(
    "import polars as pl\n"
    "\n"
    'gdp = pl.read_parquet("useful-views/gdp-per-capita.parquet")\n'
    "growth = (\n"
    '    gdp.filter(pl.col("year") >= 2000)\n'
    '    .group_by("iso", "country")\n'
    '    .agg(pl.col("growth_pct").mean().round(2).alias("avg_growth_pct"))\n'
    '    .sort("iso")\n'
    ")\n"
    'growth.write_parquet("useful-views/growth-since-2000.parquet")\n',
    encoding="utf-8",
)
```

```sh
cat recipes/growth_since_2000/recipe.toml
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
sh("cat recipes/growth_since_2000/recipe.toml")
```

```sh
cat recipes/growth_since_2000/01_average_growth.py
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
sh("cat recipes/growth_since_2000/01_average_growth.py")
```

`recipe.toml` says what the recipe makes and from what, and lists its steps
in order. The step is an ordinary script: it reads the input and writes the
output that `recipe.toml` names. [Recipes](concepts/recipes.md) and
[Steps](concepts/steps.md) cover both.

```sh
useful-views run growth_since_2000
useful-views check
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
sh("useful-views run growth_since_2000")
sh("useful-views check")
```

```{python}
#| include: false
growth = pl.read_parquet("useful-views/growth-since-2000.parquet")
assert growth.columns == ["iso", "country", "avg_growth_pct"] and growth.height == 4
```

The catalog now lists three views.

Steps are code: `run` and `sync` run the Python in `recipes/`. Read the
recipes of a project you didn't write before you run them; see
[Steps](concepts/steps.md).

## Who writes what

| You write | useful-views writes |
|---|---|
| `README.md`, `sources.toml`, and everything in `recipes/` | `datapackage.json`, `useful-views/README.md` and `cookbook.json` |

`init` and `new-recipe` start your files from templates, then leave them to
you. `init` also writes `.gitignore` and `AGENTS.md` once; after that they
are yours too. Don't edit the files useful-views writes.

## Start your own project

```sh
useful-views init my-project
```

`init` makes the same folders, empty. Put your raw files in `raw/`, then
add recipes with `useful-views new-recipe`. [Projects](concepts/projects.md)
says what to commit.
